source.title_on_document: Can AI Enhance its Creativity to Beat Humans ?

supplement.where: Section 9 Appendix, pp. 25-54 of the arXiv PDF; footnote 12 (p. 25) says the original French instructions are available upon request
supplement.holds: Task instructions and Expert AI prompts (9.1), output examples (9.2), descriptive statistics with means, SDs, and counts per agent (Tables 12-14, pp. 36-37), pairwise Wilcoxon tests (Tables 15-17, pp. 37-38), PCA (9.5), evaluator-characteristic regressions (9.6)

paper_design_summary: The authors compare creative outputs from humans (collected in two earlier experiments) with outputs from GPT-4 (Text and Alternative Uses tasks) and GPT-4 with DALL-E 2 (Draw task) under a naive prompt (the human instructions) and an expert prompt (a system prompt written by GPT-4). Of an initial pool of 201 student evaluators recruited through the Strasbourg LEES lab, 199 were retained after two dropped out before completing the experiment; they rated outputs from one task each on 0-5 criteria (validity, form, elaboration, originality, feasibility) without being told some were AI-made, and the authors add theme-based and embedding-based measures (pp. 7-8, Sections 3.2-3.3 and footnote 1). No participant used AI to produce anything.

studies.label: Text task (story with ten mandatory words): Human vs Naive AI vs Expert AI

participants.exclusions: Evaluator attrition pooled across all three tasks: two evaluators were removed from the initial pool of 201 because they dropped out before completing the experiment, leaving 199 retained evaluators (p. 8, Section 3.3 and footnote 1). Initial evaluator assignment counts by task and the task allocation of the two dropouts are not stated. These are evaluator counts, not counts of creators assigned to AI assistance; creator exclusions and distinct creator counts are not stated.
participants.who: Corpus of stories: human stories from earlier experiments (Maltese et al. 2023, Guichardaz et al. 2024) plus GPT-4 stories. Table 12 (p. 36) prints '# Observations' 85 (Naive AI), 83 (Expert AI), 84 (Human); the paper does not label these as number of authors. Rated by 70 student evaluators (Table 3, p. 8), each shown 15 texts; 330, 323, and 327 evaluations (Table 12, p. 36).
participants.country: France (University of Strasbourg evaluators; French-language outputs)
participants.quote: In the case of human data, these were collected through three different creativity tasks conducted during two experimental protocols
participants.locator: p. 6, Section 3.1; p. 8, Section 3.3 and Table 3; p. 36, Table 12

ai_tool.how_used: AI generates the outputs itself. Naive AI: user prompt with the human instructions. Expert AI: GPT-4 first writes a system prompt to amplify its creativity, then answers the instructions (p. 10, Section 5.1; prompts p. 25, Appendix 9.1.1).

task.description: Write an interesting and original story from personal memories using all ten words: walls, bricks, towers, roof, keep, stones, rampart, door, window, flag (in French).

outcomes.name: Originality rating of the story (0-5)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Student evaluators blind to AI origin, 0-5 'Originality: Unusualness of ideas' (Table 2, p. 8). Tukey HSD on ratings (Table 6); ordered logit with # Words control, Naive AI reference, with and without evaluator FE (Table 7).

contrasts.treatment_arm: Naive AI (GPT-4, human instructions as prompt)
contrasts.reported: Means: Naive AI 3.506 (1.103), Expert AI 3.728 (1.063), Human 2.972 (1.445); # Evaluations 330 / 323 / 327 (Table 12). Tukey mean difference Human vs Naive AI -0.534***, Human vs Expert AI -0.755***, Expert AI vs Naive AI 0.221* (Table 6). Ordered logit controlling # Words, Naive AI reference: Human 0.177 (0.198) col 7, 0.281 (0.206) col 8 with evaluator FE; Expert AI -0.270 (0.170), -0.368** (0.177); Observations 980 (Table 7). Table 5 summary: N = H > E.
contrasts.locator: p. 14, Tables 6 and 7; p. 36, Table 12; p. 13, Table 5

outcomes.name: Distance to centroid (group-level semantic spread of sentences)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Each sentence embedded with a French sentence model (Sentence-CamemBERT-Large); cosine distance of each sentence to the centroid of its agent type. Higher = more spread. Paper describes it as group-level semantic distance between the sentences of one agent (p. 12).

contrasts.treatment_arm: Naive AI (GPT-4, human instructions as prompt)
contrasts.reported: Tukey mean difference Distance to centroid: Expert AI vs Naive AI 0.059***, Human vs Naive AI 0.127***, Human vs Expert AI 0.068*** (Table 6); Wilcoxon gives the same differences (Table 15, p. 37). Table 5 summary: H > E > N. Arm means not printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 14, Table 6; p. 37, Table 15; p. 13, Table 5

diversity_detail.computed_over: Each sentence against the centroid of all sentences from its agent type (Human, Naive AI, Expert AI)
diversity_detail.uncertainty: ANOVA with Tukey HSD and pairwise Wilcoxon on sentence-level distances; stars only, no SEs printed
diversity_detail.notes: Higher value = more dispersed; AI outputs are less dispersed than human outputs.

studies.label: Alternative Uses task (five objects): Human vs Naive AI vs Expert AI

participants.exclusions: Evaluator attrition pooled across all three tasks: two evaluators were removed from the initial pool of 201 because they dropped out before completing the experiment, leaving 199 retained evaluators (p. 8, Section 3.3 and footnote 1). Initial evaluator assignment counts by task and the task allocation of the two dropouts are not stated. These are evaluator counts, not counts of creators assigned to AI assistance; creator exclusions and distinct creator counts are not stated.
participants.who: Corpus of idea lists: human lists from earlier experiments plus GPT-4 lists. Table 13 (p. 36) prints '# Observations' 54 per agent and '# Evaluations' 192 per agent. Rated by 64 student evaluators (Table 3, p. 8), each shown 9 outputs (p. 7).
participants.country: France (University of Strasbourg evaluators; French-language outputs)

participants.locator: p. 6, Section 3.1; p. 7, Section 3.2; p. 8, Table 3; p. 36, Table 13

ai_tool.how_used: AI generates the idea lists itself under a naive prompt (human instructions) or an expert prompt (GPT-4-written system prompt) (p. 10, Section 5.1; p. 26, Appendix 9.1.2).

task.description: List unusual uses for a brick, a cardboard box, an extension cord, a metal pipe, and a t-shirt.
task.duration: 15 minutes, three minutes per word (p. 25, Appendix 9.1.2)

outcomes.name: Originality rating of ideas (0-5)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Student evaluators blind to AI origin rate each idea 0-5 on originality (p. 7; Appendix 9.3.3). Tukey HSD (Table 8); ordered logit with mean # words per idea control, Naive AI reference (Table 9).

contrasts.treatment_arm: Naive AI (GPT-4, human instructions as prompt)
contrasts.reported: Means: Naive AI 4.427 (0.841), Expert AI 4.578 (0.697), Human 3.911 (1.24); # Evaluations 192 each (Table 13). Tukey mean difference Human vs Naive AI -0.516***, Human vs Expert AI -0.667***, Expert AI vs Naive AI 0.151 (Table 8). Ordered logit, Naive AI reference: Human -1.078*** (0.209) col 5, -1.394*** (0.230) col 6 with evaluator FE; Expert AI 0.584*** (0.222), 0.817*** (0.241); Observations 576 (Table 9).

outcomes.name: Distance to centroid (group-level semantic spread of ideas)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Each idea embedded with a French sentence model (Sentence-CamemBERT-Large); cosine distance of each idea to the centroid of its agent type. Higher = more spread.

contrasts.treatment_arm: Naive AI (GPT-4, human instructions as prompt)
contrasts.reported: Tukey mean difference Distance to centroid: Expert AI vs Naive AI 0.008, Human vs Naive AI 0.022***, Human vs Expert AI 0.015** (Table 8); Wilcoxon: 0.008, 0.022***, 0.015*** (Table 16, p. 38). Table 5 summary: H > E = N. Arm means not printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 16, Table 8; p. 38, Table 16; p. 13, Table 5

diversity_detail.computed_over: Each idea against the centroid of all ideas from its agent type
diversity_detail.uncertainty: ANOVA with Tukey HSD and pairwise Wilcoxon on idea-level distances; stars only, no SEs printed
diversity_detail.notes: Higher value = more dispersed; AI ideas are less dispersed than human ideas.

studies.label: Draw task (alien animal): Human vs Naive AI vs Expert AI

participants.exclusions: Evaluator attrition pooled across all three tasks: two evaluators were removed from the initial pool of 201 because they dropped out before completing the experiment, leaving 199 retained evaluators (p. 8, Section 3.3 and footnote 1). Initial evaluator assignment counts by task and the task allocation of the two dropouts are not stated. These are evaluator counts, not counts of creators assigned to AI assistance; creator exclusions and distinct creator counts are not stated.
participants.who: Corpus of drawings: human drawings from earlier experiments plus GPT-4/DALL-E 2 images. Table 14 (p. 37) prints '# Observations' 90 per agent and '# Evaluations' 325 per agent. Rated by 65 student evaluators (Table 3, p. 8), each shown 15 drawings.
participants.quote: In the case of human data, these were collected through three different creativity tasks conducted during two experimental protocols
participants.locator: p. 6, Section 3.1; p. 8, Table 3; p. 37, Table 14

ai_tool.how_used: AI generates the drawings itself under a naive prompt (human instructions) or an expert prompt written by GPT-4 asking for a pencil-sketch alien animal (p. 7, Section 3.1; p. 26, Appendix 9.1.3).

task.description: Imagine and draw an animal from a planet very different from Earth, front and profile, with a short description and a name.

outcomes.name: Originality rating of the drawing (0-5)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Student evaluators blind to AI origin, 0-5 originality. Tukey HSD (Table 10); ordered logit with % pixel used control, Naive AI reference (Table 11).

contrasts.treatment_arm: Naive AI (GPT-4 + DALL-E 2, human instructions as prompt)
contrasts.reported: Means: Naive AI 2.548 (1.449), Expert AI 3.797 (1.268), Human 2.554 (1.516); # Evaluations 325 each (Table 14). Tukey mean difference Human vs Naive AI 0.006, Human vs Expert AI -1.243***, Expert AI vs Naive AI 1.249*** (Table 10). Ordered logit, Naive AI reference: Human 0.200 (0.167) col 7, 0.232 (0.170) col 8 with evaluator FE; Expert AI 1.605*** (0.148), 1.786*** (0.153); Observations 975 (Table 11).
contrasts.locator: p. 17, Table 10; p. 18, Table 11; p. 37, Table 14

outcomes.name: Distance to centroid (group-level visual spread of drawings)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Each drawing is represented by a CLIP image embedding; cosine distance is measured from each drawing to the centroid of its agent type (Human, Naive AI, Expert AI). Higher values indicate greater spread across drawings. ANOVA with Tukey HSD and pairwise Wilcoxon are variants of the same outcome (p. 11, Section 5.2; p. 12, Section 5.3).

contrasts.treatment_arm: Naive AI (GPT-4 + DALL-E 2, human instructions as prompt)
contrasts.reported: Tukey mean difference Distance to centroid: Expert AI vs Naive AI -0.02***, Human vs Naive AI 0.01***, Human vs Expert AI 0.03*** (Table 10). Pairwise Wilcoxon reports the same differences and significance markers (Table 17). *** indicates significance at the 1% level. Table 5 summary: H > N > E. Centroid arm means, SEs, and a test-specific observation count are not printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 17, Table 10; p. 38, Table 17; p. 13, Table 5

diversity_detail.computed_over: Each drawing against the centroid of drawings from its agent type (Human, Naive AI, Expert AI)
diversity_detail.uncertainty: ANOVA with Tukey HSD and pairwise Wilcoxon on drawing-level distances; significance stars only, with no SEs or confidence intervals printed
diversity_detail.notes: Higher values mean greater spread. Naive AI drawings are less dispersed than human drawings; Expert AI drawings are less dispersed than both. The test-specific observation count is not stated.

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: The human-output corpus reuses data from the experimental protocols of Maltese et al. (2023) and Guichardaz et al. (2024). Exact participant overlap, task-to-source mapping, and overlap counts are not specified.
sample_overlap.quote: In the case of human data, these were collected through three different creativity tasks conducted during two experimental protocols [Maltese et al., 2023, Guichardaz et al., 2024].

eligibility.reason: AI-generated outputs (GPT-4, GPT-4 with DALL-E 2) are compared with human outputs collected in earlier experiments; no person produced output with AI help. The only random assignment is of evaluators to task pools (p. 7, Section 3.2), not of people to AI assistance. The number of distinct human creators analyzed is not explicitly reported; the '# Observations' counts describe the output corpus, so the creator sample-size criterion is unclear (p. 6, Section 3.1; pp. 36-37, Tables 12-14). The evaluator counts do not establish the number of creators (p. 8, Section 3.3 and footnote 1).

one_line_finding: Blind student evaluators rated naive-prompt GPT-4 ideas more original than human ideas on the alternative uses task (4.427 vs 3.911, Table 13, p. 36) and stories more original before but not after a text-length control (3.506 vs 2.972, Table 12, p. 36; ordered logit Human 0.177, SE 0.198, Table 7, p. 14), with no difference for drawings (2.548 vs 2.554, Table 14, p. 37), while human outputs lay farther from their group centroid in embedding space on all three tasks (Tables 6, 8, 10, pp. 14-17).
